questions.question: The Council of Ministers shall not exceed ___% of the total number of members of the Assembly of States.
questions.solution:
The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 specifies that the size of the Council of Ministers (including the CM/PM) shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly/Lok Sabha.
  • Minimum Limit: For States, the number of ministers (including the CM) shall not be less than 12.
  • Objective: This was enacted to prevent jumbo cabinets and check the misuse of ministerial berths for political gains.

questions.question: What is the structure of the Indian judiciary?
questions.solution:
The Indian Judiciary has a four-tier structure.
  • Hierarchy: 1. Supreme Court (Top) -> 2. High Courts -> 3. District Courts -> 4. Subordinate/Lower Courts.
  • Integration: Unlike the US, India has an integrated judicial system, meaning the Supreme Court's decisions bind all lower courts.

questions.question: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of _________.
questions.solution:
A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed from office by the President only after an address by Parliament on the grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity.
  • Article 124(4): This requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament (2/3 members present and voting).
  • Process: The process is regulated by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

questions.question: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court”?
questions.solution:
The writ of Habeas Corpus (literally 'to have the body') means that an arrested person must be presented before the court.
  • Purpose: It protects individual liberty against arbitrary detention by the state or private individuals.
  • Enforcement: The court examines the legality of the detention and orders release if no legal justification exists.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution as a Fundamental Duty?
questions.solution:
To respect elders is a traditional social value but is NOT mentioned as a Fundamental Duty in Article 51A.
  • Constitutional Duties: These include respecting the National Flag, safeguarding public property, and protecting the environment.
  • Total Count: There are 11 duties in total, none of which explicitly command the 'respect of elders'.

questions.question: How many rights are mentioned under “Right to Equality”?
questions.solution:
The Right to Equality encompasses 5 specific rights under Articles 14 to 18.
  • The Rights: 1. Equality before law (Art 14), 2. Prohibition of discrimination (Art 15), 3. Equality of opportunity in employment (Art 16), 4. Abolition of untouchability (Art 17), 5. Abolition of titles (Art 18).

questions.question: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there in India?
questions.solution:
There are currently 543 Lok Sabha constituencies in India for which direct elections are held.
  • Composition: 543 members are elected by the people.
  • Historical Note: Previously, 2 members could be nominated from the Anglo-Indian community, but this was abolished by the 104th Amendment Act, 2019.

questions.question: Which of the following terms is NOT included in the Preamble of Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The term 'Federalism' is not included in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
  • Preamble Terms: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.
  • Quasi-Federal: While India is federal in structure, the Preamble emphasizes unity and integrity instead.

questions.question: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 amends the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 to empower the central government to specify a _______.
questions.solution:
The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 empowers the government to specify a carbon credit trading scheme.
  • Goal: To incentivize the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.
  • Obligation: It allows the government to require designated consumers to meet a minimum share of non-fossil energy consumption.

questions.question: Which minorities are mentioned in article 30 of the Indian Contituiton?
questions.solution:
Article 30 of the Constitution mentions two types of minorities: Linguistic and Religious.
  • Right: It grants these minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
  • Protection: This ensures that minority cultures and languages are preserved through education.

questions.question: Which of the following jurisdictions of the Supreme Court allows it to settle disputes between the centre and state and amongst states?
questions.solution:
The Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Article 131) allows it to settle disputes between the Centre and States or between States.
  • Exclusive Power: Only the Supreme Court has the power to hear such federal disputes in the first instance.
  • Condition: The dispute must involve a question of law or fact on which a legal right depends.

questions.question: According to Article 51 A [a] of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every Indian citizen to abide by the ___________ and respect its ideals and institutions.
questions.solution:
Article 51A(a) states that it is the duty of every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
  • National Symbols: This clause also explicitly mentions respecting the National Flag and the National Anthem.
  • First Duty: It is chronologically the first duty listed in the Part IV-A.

questions.question: In May 2022, the Inter-State Council, which works to promote and support cooperative federalism in the country, has been reconstituted. Who will be the chairman of this council?
questions.solution:
The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Inter-State Council.
  • Article 263: The Council is a constitutional body established to support cooperative federalism.
  • Composition: It includes the PM, CMs of all states, and administrators of UTs.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the High Court?
questions.option_2: It provides advisory opinion to the President of India.
questions.option_3: It has the power of judicial review.
questions.option_4: It controls the subordinate courts within its jurisdiction.
questions.solution:
The statement that the High Court 'provides advisory opinion to the President' is INCORRECT.
  • Advisory Power: Under Article 143, only the Supreme Court provides advisory opinions to the President.
  • HC Powers: High Courts have writ jurisdiction (Art 226), judicial review, and administrative control over subordinate courts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a Fundamental Right in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Right to Property is NOT a Fundamental Right.
  • Abolition: It was removed from Part III by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
  • Current Status: It is now a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

questions.question: Which freedom is considered as the ‘Hallmark of Democracy’?
questions.solution:
Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28) is often described as the 'Hallmark of Democracy' in a diverse nation like India.
  • Secularism: It ensures that the state treats all religions equally and citizens can practice their faith without interference.
  • Core Value: It reflects the pluralistic nature of Indian society.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the eligibility criteria for being elected as Vice President of India?
questions.option_1: He/She should be a citizen of India.
questions.option_2: He/She should be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
questions.option_3: He/She should not hold any office of profit under the Union Government/state government or any subordinate local authority.
questions.option_4: He/She should have completed 35 years of age.
questions.solution:
To be eligible for Vice President, a person must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.
  • Distinction: The President must be qualified for the Lok Sabha, while the Vice President (who chairs the Rajya Sabha) must be qualified for the Rajya Sabha.
  • Other Criteria: Citizen of India, 35+ years old, and no office of profit.

questions.question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India deals with ______________.
questions.option_1: protection of life and personal liberty
questions.option_4: protection in respect of conviction for offences
questions.solution:
Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences.
  • Three Protections: 1. No ex-post-facto law, 2. No double jeopardy (punished twice for the same crime), 3. No self-incrimination (forced to be a witness against oneself).

questions.question: Which article of Indian constitution is related with the Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim?
questions.solution:
Article 371F contains special provisions for the State of Sikkim.
  • History: Sikkim became a full-fledged state of India via the 36th Amendment Act, 1975.
  • Provisions: It protects the laws, social customs, and specific rights of the people of Sikkim.

questions.question: The 73rd amendment deals with which of the following?
questions.solution:
The 73rd Amendment Act deals with the Panchayati Raj System.
  • Local Self-Govt: It gave constitutional status to rural local bodies and added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.
  • Democracy: It ensured regular elections and reservation for SCs, STs, and women at the village level.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was deleted by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
questions.solution:
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 deleted the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
  • Political Context: This was done by the Janata Government to remove property as an obstacle to land reforms and wealth redistribution.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles states that a State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them?
questions.solution:
Article 15 states that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
  • Access: It also ensures that no citizen is restricted from using shops, public restaurants, or public wells based on these grounds.
  • Exceptions: It allows the state to make special provisions for women, children, and backward classes.

questions.question: Who runs the government at the national level under the parliamentary system?
questions.option_3: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.option_4: The President and Council of Ministers
questions.solution:
In a parliamentary system, the government is run by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
  • Real Executive: They hold the actual power and are responsible to the Lok Sabha.
  • Collective Responsibility: They sink or swim together as a team.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties are contained within which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Duties are contained within Article 51A.
  • Part: They are located in Part IV-A.
  • Inspiration: Added based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.question: The Supreme Court on 18 July, 2022 ordered its registry to work out a mechanism to remove personal details of persons entangled in matrimonial litigation. This decision was taken to recognize which right as part of ‘right to privacy’?
questions.solution:
The Supreme Court recognized the 'Right to be Forgotten' as part of the 'Right to Privacy' in matrimonial litigation cases.
  • Privacy: This allows individuals to request the removal of personal details from online records to prevent permanent social stigma.
  • Puttaswamy Case: This builds on the 2017 landmark judgment that declared privacy a Fundamental Right under Article 21.

questions.question: All the ______ countries likely to have Constitution.
questions.solution:
All democratic countries are likely to have a written or unwritten Constitution.
  • Rule of Law: A constitution provides the framework to prevent the tyranny of the majority and ensures that the government acts according to established rules.

questions.question: If the State government dissolves the Panchayati Raj Institutions before the end of their five-year term, fresh elections should ordinarily be held within _____.
questions.solution:
If a Panchayat is dissolved before its 5-year term, fresh elections must be held within six months from the date of dissolution.
  • Remaining Term: The newly elected Panchayat continues only for the remainder of the period of the dissolved body.
  • Exception: If the remaining term is less than six months, no mid-term election is mandatory.

questions.question: A booklet released by the Lok Sabha Secretariat has listed out words and expressions that would be considered unparliamentary in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Which of the following words is NOT declared unparliamentary?
questions.solution:
The word 'Chakkar' was NOT listed as unparliamentary in the 2022 booklet.
  • Unparliamentary Words: These included Jumlajeevi, Shakuni, Jaichand, Nautanki, and Girgit.
  • Code of Conduct: Such words are removed (expunged) from the official records of the house if used by members.
